interactions_checked.interaction: ACE‑I can increase serum potassium; beta‑blocker may mask symptoms of hyperkalaemia. Monitor potassium and renal function.
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K+ before starting ramipril and repeat 1–2 weeks after initiation.

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure‑lowering effect may cause symptomatic hypotension.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP after dose titration; consider reducing amlodipine if BP <130/80 mmHg.

interactions_checked.interaction: Concurrent use of two statins markedly increases risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue simvastatin at least 48 h before starting atorvastatin.

interactions_checked.interaction: Sevelamer can bind calcium channel blockers and reduce their absorption.
interactions_checked.action: Take sevelamer at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after amlodipine.

interactions_checked.interaction: Sevelamer may reduce absorption of beta‑blocker.
interactions_checked.action: Separate administration by ≥1 hour before or ≥2 hours after metoprolol.

interactions_checked.interaction: Sevelamer may bind galantamine and lower its bioavailability.
ESA therapy can raise blood pressure; ACE‑I may mitigate but monitor closely.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure after each ESA dose.

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium not provided – required before initiating ramipril.
Serum calcium, phosphate, PTH not provided – needed to confirm need for sevelamer and alfacalcidol.
Hemoglobin and iron studies not provided – ESA and IV iron to be started only if Hb <100 g/L and iron deficiency confirmed.
Serum bicarbonate not provided – sodium bicarbonate to be started only if bicarbonate <20 mmol/L.
Liver function tests not provided – required before initiating high‑intensity atorvastatin.
Allergy status not provided – verify no allergy to ACE‑I, statins, sevelamer, or vitamin D analogue.
treatment_summary: The plan adds an ACE inhibitor (ramipril) for renoprotection and BP control, switches to a high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin) for cardiovascular risk reduction, and introduces phosphate binder (sevelamer), vitamin D analogue (alfacalcidol), IV iron and ESA for CKD‑related mineral bone disorder and anaemia. Sodium bicarbonate is offered if metabolic acidosis is present. All additions follow NICE NG107/NG203 recommendations, consider drug‑drug interactions, and include monitoring and safety checks.
